title: NOCO GB40 and GB50, from the maker pages
description: Peak current, engine limits, weight, and enclosure rating as the NOCO pages state them for GB40 and GB50, with a dated recall line for each.
fit: The GB40 page states 1,000 A peak current, gas engines up to 6 L, diesel engines up to 3 L, and 2.4 lb. The GB50 page states 1,500 A, gas engines up to 7 L, diesel engines up to 4.5 L, and 2.7 lb. Both pages state IP65.

If the engine size is above the limit on the GB40 line and within the limit on the GB50 line, the GB50 figures are the ones that name that size. If you are reading the lower stated weight, that figure is on the GB40 line.

title: Coway Airmega Mighty and Levoit Core 300S-P, from the maker pages
description: Size and weight as the Coway and Levoit pages state them for the AP-1512HH and the Core 300S-P, with a dated recall line for each. Specs that only one page lists stay off this table.
fit: The shared labels are dimensions and weight. Coway states 16.8 × 18.3 × 9.6 in and 12.3 lb. Levoit states 8.7 × 8.7 × 14.2 in and 7.48 lb.

CADR, room coverage, and power are on the Coway card only. Rated power, noise, and power supply are on the Levoit card only. Those rows are left out because the other card does not use the same label.

title: Lasko CT32150 and CT14401, from the maker pages
description: Heat output, voltage, height, weight, and the safety line as the Lasko pages state them for CT32150 and CT14401, with a dated recall line for each.
fit: Both pages state 900 W to 1,500 W and 120 V. The CT32150 page states 31.6 in and 5.7 lb. The CT14401 page states 14 in and 3.3 lb.

The CT32150 safety line names ETL listing, a tip-over switch, and overheat protection. The CT14401 safety line names ETL listing and overheat protection. A taller stated height is the CT32150 line. A shorter stated height and a lower stated weight are the CT14401 lines.

title: Ninja Crispi FN101 and COSORI Pro II, from the maker pages
linkLabel: Crispi and Cosori Pro II specs
description: Dimensions and weight as the Ninja and COSORI pages state them for the FN101 and the Pro II, with a dated recall line for each. Specs that only one page lists stay off this table.
fit: The shared labels are dimensions and weight. The Crispi page states 11.5 × 9.76 × 11.81 in and 14.55 lb. The Pro II page states 11.8 × 13.8 × 12.6 in and 12.3 lb.

Power, containers, and modes are on the Crispi card only. Capacity, rated power, and power supply are on the Pro II card only. Those rows are left out because the other card does not use the same label.

title: Shark AV2501S and AV2820AE, from the maker pages
linkLabel: AI Ultra and PowerDetect robot specs
description: Weight, cleaning path, dimensions, voltage, and wattage as the Shark pages state them for the AV2501S and the AV2820AE, with a dated recall line for each.
fit: The AV2501S page states 14.77 lbs, a 5.7 in cleaning path, 15.35 in L x 12.01 in W x 17.72 in H, 120 volts, and 650 watts. The AV2820AE page states 14.55 lbs, a 5.7 in cleaning path, 15.39 in L x 10.87 in W x 16.93 in H, 14.4 volts, and 35 watts.
A lower stated weight is the AV2820AE line. The voltage and wattage rows are the figures each Shark page prints for that model. Dust cup capacity is on the AV2501S card only.

title: Dyson V15 Detect Absolute and Shark IP3251, from the maker pages
linkLabel: V15 Detect and PowerDetect cordless specs
description: Weight, run time, and charge time as the Dyson and Shark pages state them for the V15 Detect Absolute and the IP3251, with a dated recall line for each.
fit: The V15 Detect Absolute page states 6.83 lb, up to 60 min of run time, and a 4.5 hr charge time. The IP3251 page states 18.47 lbs, up to 70 minutes measured at the hand vacuum in ECO mode, and a 6 hour charge time.
A lower stated weight is the V15 line. A longer stated run time is the IP3251 line. Bin volume is on the V15 card only. Dust cup capacity is on the IP3251 card only.

title: Sony WH-1000XM5 and Bose QuietComfort Ultra, from the maker pages
description: Weight, charge time, and battery life as the Sony and Bose pages state them for the WH-1000XM5 and the QuietComfort Ultra, with a dated recall line for each.
fit: The Sony specifications page states approx. 8.82 oz, a charge time of approx. 3.5 hours, and max. 30 hours with noise cancelling on or max. 40 hours with it off. The Bose specifications table states 0.56 lb, a 3 hour charge time, and up to 24 hours.

The weight lines use the units each page prints, ounces on the Sony page and pounds on the Bose page. A longer stated playback line with noise cancelling on is the Sony line. A shorter stated playback line is the Bose line. A shorter stated charge time is on the Bose specifications table.

title: Roborock Qrevo S and eufy X10 Pro Omni, from the maker pages
linkLabel: Qrevo S and X10 Pro Omni specs
description: Suction and robot dimensions as the Roborock and eufy pages state them for the Qrevo S and the X10 Pro Omni, with a dated recall line for each.
fit: The Qrevo S page states 7,000 Pa and robot dimensions of 13.78 x 13.9 x 3.80 in. The X10 Pro Omni page states 8,000 Pa and robot dimensions of 327 mm x 353 mm x 113.5 mm.

A higher stated suction figure is the X10 Pro Omni line. The dimension rows use the units each maker page prints, inches on the Roborock page and millimetres on the eufy page. Run time, robot weight, and dustbin volume are on the eufy card only. Dock dimensions, mop speed, battery, and charge time are on the Roborock card only.

title: Dyson V15 Detect Absolute and Dyson V8, from the maker pages
linkLabel: V15 Detect Absolute and V8 specs
description: Weight, run time, charge time, bin volume, and suction as the Dyson pages state them for the V15 Detect Absolute and the V8, with a dated recall line for each.
fit: The V15 Detect Absolute page states 6.83 lb, up to 60 min of run time, a 4.5 hr charge time, a 0.2 gallon bin, and 230 AW in Boost mode. The V8 page states 5.58 lb, 40 min maximum run time, a 5 hr charge time, a 0.14 gallon bin, and 115 AW in MAX mode.

A lower stated weight and a shorter stated charge time are the V15 lines. A shorter stated run time, a smaller stated bin, and a lower stated suction figure are the V8 lines. Whole-machine HEPA filtration is on the V15 card only.

title: Levoit Core 600S-P and Winix 5500-2, from the maker pages
description: CADR, weight, size, and power as the Levoit and Winix pages state them for the Core 600S-P and the 5500-2, with a dated recall line for each.
fit: The Core 600S-P specifications list states 391 CFM, 13.7 lb, 12.3 x 12.3 x 23.6 in, and 49 W at AC 120 V, 60 Hz. The 5500-2 manual states 243 dust, 246 pollen, and 232 smoke, about 15 lb, 15 x 8.2 x 23.6 in, and 70 W at 120 V / 60 Hz.

A lower stated weight and a lower stated wattage are the Core 600S-P lines. The CADR row is one CFM figure on the Levoit page and three CADR figures on the Winix page. Room coverage uses a different label on each card, so it stays off this table. Noise and filtration are on the Levoit card only.

title: Honeywell HPA300 and Coway Airmega 250, from the maker pages
description: Size, weight, CADR, and filter life as the Honeywell and Coway pages state them for the HPA300 and the Airmega 250, with a dated recall line for each.
fit: The HPA300 product details state 20.8 x 10.83 x 22.38 in, 17 lb, smoke CADR 300, dust CADR 320, pollen CADR 300, a True HEPA filter replaced once per year, and a pre-filter replaced every 3 months. The Airmega 250 specifications state 18.5 x 19.7 x 8.3 in, 20.5 lb, smoke CADR 249, dust CADR 261, pollen CADR 230, and a Max2 filter life of 1 year.

Higher stated smoke, dust, and pollen CADR figures are the HPA300 lines. A lower stated weight is the HPA300 line. Noise and the square-foot coverage lines use labels that only one card uses, so they stay off this table.

title: Litter-Robot 4 and PetSafe ScoopFree Crystal Plus, from the maker pages
linkLabel: Litter-Robot 4 and ScoopFree Crystal Plus specs
description: Power, cleaning interval, and household line as the Whisker and PetSafe pages state them for Litter-Robot 4 and the ScoopFree Crystal Plus, with a dated recall line for each.
fit: The Litter-Robot 4 page states 15 V DC, up to 8 days before emptying the waste drawer in a 1-cat household, and suitability for up to 4 cats. The ScoopFree Crystal Plus page states plug-in power, up to 30 days of cleaning, and single or multi-cat households.

A longer stated cleaning interval is the ScoopFree line. The Litter-Robot line names a waste-drawer interval for one cat. Height, footprint, entryway, and empty weight are on the Litter-Robot card only. Tray dimensions are on the ScoopFree card only.

title: Instant Pot Duo Plus and Ninja Foodi 10-in-1, from the maker pages
description: Functions, capacity, power, and dimensions as the Instant Pot and Ninja pages state them for the Duo Plus and the 10-in-1 XL Pro, with a dated recall line for each.
fit: The Duo Plus page states pressure cook, slow cook, sauté, sous vide, steam, sterilize, keep warm, rice, and yogurt, a 6 quart volume, 1,000 W at 120 V and 60 Hz, and 12.2 L x 13.4 W x 12.9 H in. The Foodi page states Air Fry, Whole Roast, Air Roast, Bake, Dehydrate, Pizza, Broil, Toast, Bagel, and Reheat, a capacity line for a 5 lb chicken and a sheet pan of vegetables, two 12 in pizzas, or a 12 lb turkey, 1,800 W, and 62.2 × 50.6 × 42.49 cm.

The capacity lines name different things: quarts on the Duo Plus page, and food that fits on the Foodi page. A lower stated wattage is the Duo Plus line. The dimension rows use the units each page prints, inches on the Instant Pot page and centimetres on the Ninja page. Warranty is on the Foodi card only.

title: Brita Tahoe Elite and ZeroWater ZP-010, from the maker pages
description: Capacity and weight as the Brita and ZeroWater pages state them for the Tahoe Elite and the ZP-010, with a dated recall line for each.
fit: The Tahoe Elite page states a 10 cup capacity and 1.5 lb. The ZP-010 page titles a 10 cup pitcher, and the specifications table states 4 lb.

Both capacity lines say 10 cup. A lower stated weight is the Tahoe Elite line. Height, width, and filter life are on the Brita card only. Dimensions, certifications, and the included TDS meter are on the ZeroWater card only.

title: Roomba Combo j9+ and Roborock Qrevo S, from the maker pages
linkLabel: Combo j9+ and Qrevo S specs
description: Robot size, dock size, and battery as the iRobot and Roborock pages state them for the Combo j9+ and the Qrevo S, with a dated recall line for each.
fit: The Combo j9+ page states robot dimensions of 3.4 x 13.7 x 13.7 in, dock dimensions of 15.8 in W x 16.4 in D x 16.3 in H, and a lithium-ion battery. The Qrevo S page states robot dimensions of 13.78 x 13.9 x 3.80 in, dock dimensions of 13.38 x 19.17 x 20.51 in, and a 14.4 V/5200 mAh lithium-ion battery.

The battery line on the Roomba page names the chemistry. The battery line on the Roborock support sheet names voltage and capacity. Robot weight and dock weight are on the Roomba card only. Suction, mop speed, and charge time are on the Qrevo S card only.

title: AirPods Pro 3 and Shokz OpenRun Pro 2, from the maker pages
linkLabel: AirPods Pro 3 and OpenRun Pro 2 specs
description: Play time and ingress rating as the Apple and Shokz pages state them for AirPods Pro 3 and the OpenRun Pro 2, with a dated recall line for each.
fit: The AirPods Pro page states up to 8 hours of listening with Active Noise Cancellation and an IP57 rating. The OpenRun Pro 2 page states up to 12 hours of play time and an IP55 rating.

A longer stated play line is the OpenRun Pro 2 line. The rating row is IP57 on the Apple page and IP55 on the Shokz page. Hearing Aid listening time and a heart-rate sensor are on the AirPods card only. Quick charge and drivers are on the Shokz card only.

title: EGO SNT2110 and Toro Power Clear 38753, from the maker pages
description: Clearing width and throw as the EGO and Toro pages state them for the SNT2110 and the Power Clear 38753, with a dated recall line for each.
fit: The EGO page states a clearing width of 21 in and a throw of up to 40 ft. The Toro 38753 page states a clearing width of 21 in and a throw of up to 35 ft.
Those two labels are the shared rows. Engine, intake height, and weight are on the Toro card only. Auger, power, and tool warranty are on the EGO card only.

sections.heading: The width row does not separate them
paragraphs: Both maker pages print 21 in on the clearing-width line. A reader who stops at width has not found a difference. The throw line is the shared row that does differ. The EGO page prints up to 40 ft. The Toro page prints up to 35 ft. Both are the maker’s own “up to” wording.

The units match, inches for width and feet for throw, so the rows can sit in one table. A longer stated throw, at the same stated width, is the EGO line. A shorter stated throw is the Toro line. Neither throw line names a snow depth, a slope, or a wind speed.

sections.heading: Pick by the lines that stay off the table
paragraphs: Pick the EGO page if the decision turns on a battery power line at that 21 in width. The EGO page states that Peak Power uses two 56V ARC Lithium batteries, names a steel auger, and states a 5-year limited tool warranty. Those labels are not on the Toro card, so they are not in the table. Pick the EGO page as well if the throw figure you are matching is the longer one, up to 40 ft.

Pick the Toro page if the decision turns on a gas-engine line at the same stated width. The Toro page states a 212 cc engine, an intake height of 12.5 in, and a weight of 84 lb, with a throw of up to 35 ft. Intake height and weight are Toro-only labels. A stated weight of 84 lb is the figure to read if you are matching a walk-behind machine rather than a battery tool.

The auger material and the battery description answer a different question from the engine displacement. Read the label that matches the power source you already have. A two-battery 56V line and a 212 cc line are not the same kind of spec, which is why they stay in the cards and out of the shared table.

sections.heading: Older Power Clear notices are a model-number question
paragraphs: The recall block on this page is the catalogue match for SNT2110 and for 38753. Open each model page for the feed link. The Toro card also links older Power Clear notices. The 2010 CPSC notice names Power Clear 180 models 38272 and 38282. The 2011 CPSC notice names snowblower models 38588 and 38589, plus a mower model. The catalogue model on this page is 38753, which is not one of those model numbers.

Health Canada’s 2010 notice names the same Power Clear 180 models, 38272 and 38282. Health Canada’s 2011 notice names 38588 and 38589. Read the model and serial decal the notice describes before treating 38753 as one of those machines. The EGO card does not carry those Toro notices.

title: Snow Joe 24V-SS10 and EGO SNT2110, from the maker pages
description: Clearing width and throw as the Snow Joe manual and the EGO page state them for the 24V-SS10 and the SNT2110, with a dated recall line for each.
fit: The Snow Joe manual states a clearing width of 10 in and a throw of up to 20 ft. The EGO page states a clearing width of 21 in and a throw of up to 40 ft.
Battery, snow depth, and weight are on the Snow Joe card only. Auger, power, and tool warranty are on the EGO card only.

sections.heading: Width and throw are different kinds of machine
paragraphs: The shared labels are clearing width and throw, and both numbers differ. The Snow Joe manual prints 10 in and up to 20 ft. The EGO page prints 21 in and up to 40 ft. A wider stated path and a longer stated throw are the EGO lines. A narrower stated path and a shorter stated throw are the Snow Joe lines.

The Snow Joe manual also states a 24 V max, 4.0 Ah battery, snow depth up to 6 in, and a weight of 9.9 lb. Those labels are not on the EGO card. The EGO page states a steel auger, Peak Power from two 56V ARC Lithium batteries, and a 5-year limited tool warranty. Those labels are not on the Snow Joe card. The table leaves them out because a shared table only repeats a label both pages use.

sections.heading: Pick by path, depth, and weight
paragraphs: Pick the Snow Joe manual if the path you are matching is 10 in, the stated snow depth is up to 6 in, and the stated weight is 9.9 lb. That combination is a shovel-sized cordless tool. The throw line that goes with it is up to 20 ft. The battery line on that manual is 24 V max, 4.0 Ah, which is a different voltage line from the EGO page.

Pick the EGO page if the path you are matching is 21 in and the throw line you are matching is up to 40 ft. The power line on that page names two 56V batteries, and the auger line names steel. Those are the figures to read for a walk-behind cordless blower rather than a 10 in shovel.

A 9.9 lb stated weight and an unstated EGO weight cannot share a weight row. If weight is the deciding line, it is on the Snow Joe card. If auger material is the deciding line, it is on the EGO card. The recall block below is the catalogue match for each model, not a ranking of the two tools.

title: Blueair Blue Pure 211i Max and Coway Airmega 250, from the maker pages
description: Dimensions and weight as the Blueair and Coway pages state them for the Blue Pure 211i Max and the Airmega 250, with a dated recall line for each.
fit: The Blueair page states 22.7 x 14.4 x 14.4 in and 16.2 lb. The Airmega 250 specifications state 18.5 x 19.7 x 8.3 in and 20.5 lb.
A lower stated weight is the Blueair line. Room coverage, sound, CADR, noise, and filter life use labels that only one card uses, so they stay off this table.

sections.heading: The shared rows are the cabinet, not the airflow
paragraphs: Dimensions and weight are the labels both pages print. Blueair states a 22.7 x 14.4 x 14.4 in cabinet at 16.2 lb. Coway states an 18.5 x 19.7 x 8.3 in cabinet at 20.5 lb. A lower stated weight is the Blueair line. The shape lines are not the same proportions: one page is closer to a square footprint, and the other prints a shallower 8.3 in side.

Airflow is not a shared label. The Blueair page states a recommended room of 674 sq ft and sound of 23 to 53 dB. The Coway page states coverage of 465 sq ft at 4 air changes per hour, a large-room line of 1,860 sq ft at 1 air change per hour, noise of 22 to 54 dB(A), smoke CADR 249, dust CADR 261, pollen CADR 230, and a Max2 filter life of 1 year. Those lines stay on the cards because the other page does not use the same label.

sections.heading: Pick by the room line you can actually cite
paragraphs: Pick the Blueair page if the room figure you are matching is the 674 sq ft recommended line, and the cabinet you are matching is 22.7 x 14.4 x 14.4 in at 16.2 lb. The sound line on that page is a range, 23 to 53 dB, which is a different label from Coway’s noise line.

Pick the Airmega 250 page if the figures you are matching are the CADR trio, the 4-air-change coverage of 465 sq ft, or the 1-year Max2 filter line. The stated weight on that page is 20.5 lb, higher than the Blueair weight line. The noise line is 22 to 54 dB(A). Do not treat the Blueair decibel range and the Coway decibel range as one table row. The pages do not share that label.

A square-foot line with no air-change rate and a square-foot line that names 4 air changes per hour are not the same claim. Read the sentence the maker printed. The recall block is the catalogue match for each model on the check date.

title: Levoit Core 300S-P and Core 600S-P, from the maker pages
description: Noise and weight as the Levoit pages state them for the Core 300S-P and the Core 600S-P, with a dated recall line for each.
fit: The Core 300S-P manual states noise of 22–54.5 dB and a weight of 7.48 lb. The Core 600S-P page states noise of 26–55 dB (as low as 26 dB per the maker) and a weight of 13.7 lb / 6.2 kg.

A lower stated weight is the Core 300S-P line. The 600S-P noise line is 26–55 dB (as low as 26 dB per the maker). The 300S-P noise line is 22–54.5 dB. Power, size, CADR, and room size use labels that only one card uses.

sections.heading: Same brand, two cabinets
paragraphs: Both cards are Levoit Core models, and the shared labels are noise and weight. The 300S-P manual prints 22–54.5 dB and 7.48 lb, with dimensions of 8.7 × 8.7 × 14.2 in and rated power of 39 W at AC 120 V, 60 Hz. The 600S-P page prints 26–55 dB (as low as 26 dB per the maker) and 13.7 lb / 6.2 kg, with a size of 12.3 x 12.3 x 23.6 in and power of 49 W at AC 120 V, 60 Hz.

CADR on the 600S-P page is 391 CFM. Room size on that page is 2,909 sq ft at 1 air change per hour, or 606 sq ft at 4.8. The 300S-P card does not use a CADR label or a room-size label, so those rows stay off the table. Filtration on the 600S-P page says 3-stage. That label is not on the 300S-P card.

sections.heading: Pick the smaller stated weight or the CADR line
paragraphs: Pick the Core 300S-P manual if the weight you are matching is 7.48 lb and the cabinet you are matching is 8.7 × 8.7 × 14.2 in. The power line that goes with that cabinet is 39 W. The noise line is 22–54.5 dB.

Pick the Core 600S-P page if the figure you are matching is 391 CFM, the room line that names 606 sq ft at 4.8 air changes, or the taller cabinet of 12.3 x 12.3 x 23.6 in. The stated weight on that page is 13.7 lb, and the noise line is 26–55 dB (as low as 26 dB per the maker). A lower stated wattage is the 300S-P line, 39 W against 49 W, and those power labels are not identical, so wattage stays on the cards.

Both noise lines are ranges. The 600S-P page prints 26–55 dB (as low as 26 dB per the maker). The 300S-P manual prints 22–54.5 dB. Read the range the page prints before comparing the low ends. The recall lines below are the catalogue match for each model.

title: Waterdrop G3P600 and APEC ROES-50, from the maker pages
description: Stages and capacity as the Waterdrop and APEC pages state them for the G3P600 and the ROES-50, with a dated recall line for each.
fit: The Waterdrop page states 8 stages and a capacity of 600 gallons per day. The APEC page states 5 stages and a capacity of 50 gallons per day at 60 psi.
A higher stated stage count and a higher stated daily capacity are the Waterdrop lines. Ratio and certifications are on the Waterdrop card only. Tank and dimensions are on the APEC card only.

sections.heading: Both pages name stages and a daily capacity
paragraphs: The shared labels are stages and capacity. Waterdrop prints 8 stages and 600 gallons per day. APEC prints 5 stages and 50 gallons per day at 60 psi. The APEC capacity line includes a pressure, 60 psi. The Waterdrop capacity line does not print a pressure in that field. The numbers are both “gallons per day,” and the APEC line is the one that names the test pressure.

Waterdrop also states a 2:1 pure-to-drain ratio and certifications of NSF/ANSI 42, 58, and 372. APEC also states a 4 gallon tank and dimensions of 15.5 in L x 5.25 in W x 17 in H. Those labels are not shared, so the table leaves them on the cards.

sections.heading: Pick by daily gallons, tank, or the certification line
paragraphs: Pick the Waterdrop page if the capacity figure you are matching is 600 gallons per day, the stage count you are matching is 8, or you need the 2:1 pure-to-drain line and the NSF/ANSI 42, 58, and 372 line. Those last two are Waterdrop-only labels.

Pick the APEC page if the capacity figure you are matching is 50 gallons per day at 60 psi, the stage count is 5, or you need the 4 gallon tank line and the 15.5 x 5.25 x 17 in dimension line. A tankless reading of the Waterdrop card is not a tank spec. The APEC page is the one that states a tank volume.

A stage count is not a list of contaminants. The pages state how many stages they count. They do not, in these fields, name the same contaminant table. Read the certification line where a page prints one. The recall block is the catalogue match for each system.

title: Roomba Combo j9+ and eufy X10 Pro Omni, from the maker pages
linkLabel: Combo j9+ and X10 Pro Omni specs
description: Robot weight and robot dimensions as the iRobot and eufy pages state them for the Combo j9+ and the X10 Pro Omni, with a dated recall line for each.
fit: The Combo j9+ page states a robot weight of 8.9 lb and robot dimensions of 3.4 x 13.7 x 13.7 in. The X10 Pro Omni service page states a robot weight of 4,560 g and robot dimensions of 327 mm x 353 mm x 113.5 mm.

The weight and dimension rows use the units each page prints, pounds and inches on the iRobot page and grams and millimetres on the eufy page. Battery and dock size are on the Roomba card only. Suction, run time, and dustbin volume are on the eufy card only.

sections.heading: The shared rows do not share a unit
paragraphs: Robot weight and robot dimensions are the labels both pages use. iRobot prints 8.9 lb and 3.4 x 13.7 x 13.7 in. eufy prints 4,560 g and 327 mm x 353 mm x 113.5 mm. This table does not convert those units. A reader who wants one unit has to do that arithmetic outside the maker’s sentence.

The Roomba page also states a lithium-ion battery, dock dimensions of 15.8 in W x 16.4 in D x 16.3 in H, and a dock weight of 21.9 lb. The eufy page also states 8,000 Pa suction, a run time of 173 min vacuum or 136 min vacuum and mop on standard, and a 330 ml dustbin. None of those labels are on both cards.

sections.heading: Pick by dock lines or by the suction line
paragraphs: Pick the Combo j9+ page if the figures you are matching are the inch dimensions of the robot, the 8.9 lb robot weight, or the dock at 15.8 in by 16.4 in by 16.3 in and 21.9 lb. The battery line on that page names the chemistry, lithium-ion, and does not print a milliamp-hour figure.

Pick the X10 Pro Omni page if the figure you are matching is 8,000 Pa, the run-time line of 173 minutes vacuum or 136 minutes vacuum and mop on standard, or the 330 ml dustbin. The robot weight on that page is 4,560 g, and the dimensions are in millimetres. A dock weight is not on the eufy card used here.

The Canadian catalogue note on the Roomba card links a Clean Base notice for the Roomba i7+, which is a different model name from Combo j9+. Read that notice’s model line before applying it to C975020. The recall block below is the catalogue match for each robot on the check date.

title: Dyson V15 Detect Absolute and Tineco PURE ONE S15 PRO, from the maker pages
linkLabel: V15 Detect Absolute and PURE ONE S15 PRO specs
description: Weight, run time, and charge time as the Dyson and Tineco pages state them for the V15 Detect Absolute and the PURE ONE S15 PRO, with a dated recall line for each.
fit: The V15 Detect Absolute page states 6.83 lb, up to 60 min of run time, and a 4.5 hr charge time. The PURE ONE S15 PRO page states 6.8 lbs, a run time of 40 min, and a charge time of 4 hours.

A longer stated run time is the V15 line. A shorter stated charge time is the Tineco line. Bin volume, filtration, and suction are on the V15 card only. Battery capacity and dust capacity are on the Tineco card only.

sections.heading: Three shared labels, close weights
paragraphs: Weight, run time, and charge time are the labels both pages print. Dyson states 6.83 lb, up to 60 min, and 4.5 hrs. Tineco states 6.8 lbs, 40 min, and 4 hours. The weight lines are close and use pounds on both pages. The run-time lines are not close: up to 60 min on the Dyson page, 40 min on the Tineco page.

Dyson also states a 0.2 gallon bin, whole-machine HEPA filtration, and 230 AW in Boost mode. Tineco also states a 2500 mAh battery and a dust capacity of 0.47 L. Bin volume and dust capacity are different labels and different units, so they stay off the shared table.

sections.heading: Pick by run time, charge time, or the filtration line
paragraphs: Pick the V15 Detect Absolute page if the run-time figure you are matching is up to 60 min, the suction figure you are matching is 230 AW in Boost mode, or the filtration line you need is whole-machine HEPA. The charge line that goes with that page is 4.5 hrs. The bin line is 0.2 gallon.

Pick the PURE ONE S15 PRO page if the run-time figure you are matching is 40 min, the charge line is 4 hours, or you need the 2500 mAh battery line and the 0.47 L dust-capacity line. The stated weight, 6.8 lbs, sits next to Dyson’s 6.83 lb. Both weights are as the maker pages state them.

A Health Canada notice linked from the Dyson V15 card names a FirstPower replacement battery for Dyson V6 series vacuums. That notice names V6, not the V15 Detect Absolute. Read the model on the notice before applying it here. The recall block is the catalogue match for each cordless vacuum.

title: Shark IP3251 and Tineco PURE ONE S15 PRO, from the maker pages
linkLabel: IP3251 and PURE ONE S15 PRO specs
description: Weight, run time, and charge time as the Shark and Tineco pages state them for the IP3251 and the PURE ONE S15 PRO, with a dated recall line for each.
fit: The IP3251 page states 18.47 lbs, up to 70 minutes measured at the hand vacuum in ECO mode, and a 6 hour charge time. The PURE ONE S15 PRO page states 6.8 lbs, a run time of 40 min, and a charge time of 4 hours.

A lower stated weight and a shorter stated charge time are the Tineco lines. A longer stated run time is the Shark line, and that line names the hand vacuum in ECO mode. Dust cup, dimensions, and voltage are on the Shark card only. Battery capacity and dust capacity are on the Tineco card only.

sections.heading: The run-time lines name different setups
paragraphs: The shared labels are weight, run time, and charge time. Shark prints 18.47 lbs, up to 70 minutes measured at the hand vacuum in ECO mode, and 6 hours. Tineco prints 6.8 lbs, 40 min, and 4 hours. The Shark run-time sentence names a configuration, the hand vacuum in ECO mode. The Tineco run-time field prints 40 min without that phrase.

Shark also states a 0.7 qt dust cup, dimensions of 10.24 in L x 18.5 in W x 46.46 in H, and 21.6 volts. Tineco also states a 2500 mAh battery and a 0.47 L dust capacity. Dust cup and dust capacity are different labels, so they stay off the table.

sections.heading: Pick by weight or by the ECO-mode sentence
paragraphs: Pick the IP3251 page if the run-time sentence you are matching is up to 70 minutes at the hand vacuum in ECO mode, or you need the 0.7 qt dust cup, the 21.6 volt line, and the full-size dimensions. The stated weight on that page is 18.47 lbs, and the charge line is 6 hours.

Pick the PURE ONE S15 PRO page if the weight you are matching is 6.8 lbs, the charge line is 4 hours, or you need the 2500 mAh battery and the 0.47 L dust capacity. The run-time figure on that page is 40 min, shorter than the Shark ECO-mode line.

The Shark cards in this catalogue link a 2015 CPSC notice for Shark Rotator Lift-Away vacuums. That notice names NV650W, NV651, NV652, and NV660. IP3251 is not one of those model numbers. The Health Canada notice from the same date names NV650W and NV652. Read the sticker the notice describes. The recall block below is the catalogue match for IP3251 and for the S15 PRO.

title: PetSafe Drinkwell Platinum and Pioneer Pet Raindrop 6023, from the maker pages
description: Capacity, dimensions, and material as the PetSafe and Pioneer Pet pages state them for the Drinkwell Platinum and the Raindrop 6023, with a dated recall line for each.
fit: The Drinkwell Platinum page states 168 oz, dimensions of 15.8 × 10.3 × 10.0 in, and a BPA-free material line that includes top-shelf dishwasher safe. The Raindrop 6023 page states 60 oz, dimensions of 11.75 x 9.75 x 4.25 in, and 18/8 stainless steel, dishwasher safe.
A larger stated capacity is the Drinkwell line. A smaller stated footprint is the Raindrop line. Power is on the Drinkwell card only. Weight and filter are on the Raindrop card only.

sections.heading: Capacity and the bowl material
paragraphs: Capacity, dimensions, and material are the shared labels. PetSafe prints 168 oz, 15.8 × 10.3 × 10.0 in, and BPA-free, top-shelf dishwasher safe. Pioneer Pet prints 60 oz, 11.75 x 9.75 x 4.25 in, and 18/8 stainless steel, dishwasher safe. A larger stated capacity is the Drinkwell line. A lower stated height, 4.25 in against 10.0 in, is the Raindrop line.

The material sentences are not the same claim. One page names a BPA-free plastic description and top-shelf dishwasher safe. The other names 18/8 stainless steel and dishwasher safe. Both say dishwasher safe. Only the Raindrop page names a steel grade in that field.

sections.heading: Pick by ounces, height, or the filter line
paragraphs: Pick the Drinkwell Platinum page if the capacity you are matching is 168 oz, or the power line you need is plug-in. The cabinet on that page is 15.8 × 10.3 × 10.0 in. Weight is not on that card.

Pick the Raindrop 6023 page if the capacity you are matching is 60 oz, the material line you need names 18/8 stainless steel, or you need the stated weight of 1.7 lb and the replaceable charcoal filter line. The dimensions on that page are 11.75 x 9.75 x 4.25 in, a shorter stated height than the Drinkwell line.

A charcoal filter line is not a purification certification. The Raindrop page says the filter is replaceable charcoal. It does not, in these fields, name an NSF standard. The recall block is the catalogue match for each fountain.

title: Whisker Feeder-Robot and PetSafe Simply Feed, from the maker pages
description: Portions and power as the Whisker and PetSafe pages state them for the Feeder-Robot and the Simply Feed, with a dated recall line for each.
fit: The Feeder-Robot page states portions of 1/8 cup to 1 cup and a backup battery. The Simply Feed page states portions of 1/8 to 4 cups and battery power.
A wider stated portion range, up to 4 cups, is the Simply Feed line. Meals and warranty are on the Feeder-Robot card only. Capacity, schedule, and dimensions are on the Simply Feed card only.

sections.heading: The shared rows are portion size and power
paragraphs: Portions and power are the labels both pages print. Whisker states 1/8 cup to 1 cup and a backup battery. PetSafe states 1/8 to 4 cups and battery. The low end of both portion lines is 1/8. The high end differs: 1 cup on the Feeder-Robot page, 4 cups on the Simply Feed page.

Whisker also states up to 8 scheduled meals a day and a warranty of 12 months included. PetSafe also states a 24 cup capacity, up to 12 meals a day, and dimensions of 19.0 x 9.0 x 12.5 in. Meal-count labels are not the same string on the two cards, “Meals” against “Schedule,” so the meal lines stay off the table even though both pages talk about meals.

sections.heading: Pick by hopper size or by the meal count
paragraphs: Pick the Feeder-Robot page if the portion cap you are matching is 1 cup, the meal line you are matching is up to 8 scheduled meals a day, or the power line you need says backup battery. The warranty line on that page is 12 months included. A hopper capacity in cups is not on that card.

Pick the Simply Feed page if the portion cap you are matching is 4 cups, the schedule line is up to 12 meals a day, or you need the 24 cup capacity and the 19.0 x 9.0 x 12.5 in dimensions. The power line on that page says battery, without the word backup.

A backup-battery line and a battery line are both power labels, which is why they share a row, and they are not the same sentence. Read the word the page prints. The recall block is the catalogue match for each feeder.
